leads.title: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018)
leads.documents: Supreme Court ruling striking down Section 377 as unconstitutional; legalizes same-sex sexual activity in India including Kerala on grounds of autonomy, intimacy and identity.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India' decided 6 September 2018; no URL shown in provided excerpt

leads.title: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India (2014)
leads.documents: Supreme Court ruling recognizing 'third gender', affirming transgender freedom from discrimination and right to equality; basis for Kerala's follow-up policy.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India' from 2014; no URL shown in provided excerpt

leads.title: Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019
leads.documents: Federal law banning unfair discrimination against transgender people in education, employment, healthcare, public goods/services, movement, property, office-holding, and establishments.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Adopted in 2019, the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019'; no URL shown in provided excerpt

leads.title: Kerala Government Transgender Policy, 2015
leads.documents: State policy - first in India after NALSA ruling - allowing identification as 'male', 'female' or 'TG', and providing for equal access to resources, equal treatment, life/liberty/justice and non-discrimination.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'government transgender policy in 2015' and 'policy for transgender people, which was introduced in 2015'; no URL shown in provided excerpt

leads.title: Kerala Government proposal for free gender affirmation surgery (2016) and reimbursement/scholarship scheme
leads.documents: State welfare machinery for trans health: proposed free sex reassignment surgeries in government hospitals, reimbursement for surgeries, and scholarship scheme for transgender students classes 7-10; documents implementation gaps.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'in 2016, proposed implementing free gender affirmation surgery through government hospitals' and reimbursement/scholarship discussion; no URL shown in provided excerpt

leads.title: Naz Foundation v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi (2009)
leads.documents: Delhi High Court decision finding Section 377 and prohibitions on private adult consensual non-commercial same-sex conduct violate fundamental rights; start of decriminalization timeline.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Delhi High Court decision in Naz Foundation v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi' in 2009; no URL shown in provided excerpt

leads.title: Supreme Court orders of 11 December 2013 and 2 February 2016 on Section 377
leads.documents: 2013 reversal by Justices G. S. Singhvi and S. J. Mukhopadhaya overturning 2009 decriminalization and 2014 dismissal of review, then 2016 decision to review criminalisation; enforcement history.
leads.detail: Cited in text with judges' names and dates '11 December 2013', '28 January 2014', '2 February 2016'; no URL shown in provided excerpt

leads.title: Government Medical College Hospital, Kottayam transgender clinic and District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) proposal (2017)
leads.documents: First government clinic exclusively for transgender community with specialist panel, also open to sex workers; shows rights/health machinery and DLSA role after health-concerns campaign.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Government Medical College Hospital in Kottayam opened a clinic in 2017' proposal 'put forward by the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA)'; no URL shown in provided excerpt

leads.title: Kerala DGP directive on police harassment and High Court of Kerala December 2023 observation on cyber attacks
leads.documents: Enforcement: rise in police harassment when trans people file complaints leading to DGP direction to address grievances without delay; High Court describing cyber attacks against LGBT+ as 'serious issue' and Malappuram October 2023 pride march attack leading to lathicharge.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'direction by the DGP to address their grievances without delay' and 'In December 2023, the High Court of Kerala described the cyber attacks... as a serious issue' plus Malappuram attack; no URL shown in provided excerpt
